correctness.rationale: In every geometric chart, the factored partial derivatives classify exactly 65 rational solutions; six symmetry orbit representatives have Hessian determinants 1,1,4,4,4,4 in suitable charts, proving all are A1 nodes. Exact exhaustive finite-field counts are 91 over F5 and 1651 over F25 (two unrelated nonsquare models) and 17251 over F125 (third-degree check). On the smooth minimal resolution, rational-double-point adjunction and Noether give b2=106 and b1=b3=0; 65 rational exceptional P1 curves add 65q points. The second Frobenius trace equals 106*25, saturating the Weil bound, which forces all square-eigenvalues 25 and hence multiplicities 92 at +5 and 14 at -5. Subtracting exceptional classes proves the all-n zeta. No finite sampling is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a geometrically forced reduction at the unique ramified prime of the coefficient ring of a distinguished maximal-nodal sextic. All 65 nodes remaining distinct and already rational over the smallest field is a natural, nontrivial arithmetic phenomenon. The cohomological saturation gives the entire zeta function and an exceptionally constrained Frobenius spectrum, a structural invariant not supplied by complex nodal geometry or the standard square-coordinate description.
